label: copy-phase echo of 1/a/y/w in long sequences, mid and final recall positions
explanation: Very sparse update-gate unit (0.27% of steps). Almost all mass (99%) is in the copy phase, where it fires when the fed-back input token is one of a small set: digit 1 (52% of mass), a (25%), y (13%), w (5%). It is strongly modulated by length and position: L=9 holds 75% of mass and L=8 19%, with nothing at L<=4. It peaks at recall_idx 3-4 and again at 7-8, i.e. t=12,13,16,17. The largest activations are 1 or a at recall_idx 3-4 in L=9 sequences. Rate rises with how many digits the sequence contains, and a preceding digit or l/z/x/c helps a bit. It never fires in the original phase and almost never on <DEL>. Precision is low (~16%): most copy-phase 1/a/y/w steps at these positions do not fire, and history variables did not separate them cleanly. The predicate covers ~80% of mass.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=1 (+7.60), phase=2 & in_tok=a (+6.29), phase=2 & in_tok=y (+5.48), phase=2 & in_tok=w (+4.40), phase=2 & in_tok=c (+3.03), out_tok=t (+2.68). Lower it: out_tok=h (-3.10), prev_tok=<DEL> (-2.75), recall_idx=1 (-2.75), prev_tok=e (-2.60).
